correctness.rationale: For each rule the local 8-neighbor 3-bit column map is specified without approximation. Closed spatial walks of length n in the 3-time-slice transfer graph are exactly global fixed points of the third iterate for all n>=3. The complete graph has 262144 vertices; exhaustive SCC computation gives only nontrivial components of sizes 30 and 27, 57 total cyclic vertices, all temporally constant. Life has 294072 edges; HighLife has 321875. An independent Python/NetworkX construction reproduces these results and a separate binary-state simulation finds no period-three configurations for n=3..7 in either rule. The latter is only a cross-check, not an infinite proof.

value.rationale: Conway Life has a foundational planar period-three oscillator (pulsar), so a uniform no-period-three theorem under three-row periodic confinement is a motivated dynamical boundary, not a random finite test. The result establishes an exact all-circumference temporal exclusion simultaneously in B3/S23 and its B6-extension B36/S23, despite already known period-two motion on suitable three-row Life tori. The finite graph proves the stronger structural fact that every cyclic three-layer history is time-constant, explaining the exclusion. No broad odd-period or minimal-width assertion is inferred.
